$comment: Tier definitions and service-level objectives for the pressure-test harness.
Pressure scenarios run only against the isolated EC2 clone. Live dev-site
correctness is covered separately by pressure/api-test.mjs.
The SLO numbers are v1 estimates derived from the architecture (single-process
Node, synchronous better-sqlite3, one writer, bcrypt cost 12, RSA URL signing).
Recalibrate them from the first real clone run — see README 'Calibration'.

ec2-clone.label: Isolated EC2 clone of production
ec2-clone.answers: What is the real capacity, the breaking point, and the recovery behaviour?
ec2-clone.notes: Boots from a snapshot of production's root volume, then runs a fail-closed sanitize stage before Docker starts. Load is generated from a SECOND instance in the same AZ so k6 never competes for the single CPU the app is bottlenecked on.

slo.$comment: p95/p99 in milliseconds. 'designed' status codes are excluded from error rates — see k6/lib/metrics.js.

student_quiz_start.$why: Signs one URL per question figure AND per image answer choice. With CloudFront configured each signature is an RSA-SHA1 operation on the event loop, so this scales with (figures + image options), not with question count alone.

student_quiz_submit.$why: Grades inside a transaction that holds SQLite's single write lock, then creates an ExamResult and opens a fresh queue DB handle to enqueue. Under a submit clump this is a queue, not a parallel workload.

teacher_quiz_stats.$why: Aggregates every attempt and answer row for the quiz in-process (src/lib/quiz-stats-server.ts).

admin_resources.$why: readSpool() is SYNCHRONOUS: readFileSync + line-parse of every node's NDJSON file, on the main thread. At 4 nodes x 1 sample/min x 7 days retention that is ~40k lines parsed per request, blocking the event loop for every other in-flight request.

login.$why: bcryptjs cost 12. bcryptjs is a PURE JS implementation, so unlike native bcrypt it does not release the event loop while hashing.

event_loop_delay.$why: The leading indicator for this architecture and invisible from outside the process. Every DB query is a synchronous better-sqlite3 call, so request concurrency becomes event-loop queueing rather than database parallelism. If this is healthy and latency is bad, the bottleneck is not the app.

sqlite_busy.$why: better-sqlite3 is opened with timeout: 5000 (src/lib/prisma.ts). A busy error means a write waited more than five seconds for the single write lock — i.e. a graded submission was LOST, not merely slow. Any non-zero value fails the run.

unexpected_errors.$why: Designed responses (401/403/409/410/429) are counted separately. Only genuinely unexpected statuses and transport failures fail a run.
